data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The generator is likely UNFAIR over 10000 draws because 2^31 mod 6 = 2, so the mod-6 reduction splits the 2^31 states unevenly across faces, and the deterministic LCG trajectory over 10000 terms may not correct this structural bias.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the actual simulated counts all fall within two standard deviations of 10000/6, the unfairness claim is refuted by the evidence.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the LCG's trajectory over 10000 terms happens to correct the structural mod-6 bias by chance, the generator may be fair within this window despite the theoretical bias.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the bias is too small (on the order of 1 part in 2^31) to move counts by more than a fraction of a standard deviation over 10000 draws, the unfairness claim is practically vacuous.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"A modulus of 2^31 is congruent to 2 mod 6, so reducing X mod 6 after a mod-2^31 step cannot map states to faces with exact equal frequency. The full-period distribution has a slight bias favoring faces 1 and 2 (which get one extra residue class). Over a single trajectory of 10000 terms, this structural bias persists and is unlikely to be fully compensated by the specific seed's traversal pattern, making a count excursion beyond two standard deviations plausible.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
